title: would it be possible to feed an ai the source code of stoneheart and have it re-create the game in unity or godot for personal playing and enjoyment?
author: M4ldarc
selftext:
stoneheart is a colony sim game developed by radiant entertainment and it was abandoned, and i really love the game, but there are some things that bug me out that couldnt really be fixed with mods, the game itself has its sorce code, art and textures aviable in the game files as a mod that is run by the engine like a shell, so i wondered if i could give that source code and textures to an ai and have it recreate the game in unity for example, so i can play it privately.

if so, how could it be done?

comments.author: TheMightyOscar
comments.body:
If it’s open source just do it, if not you will have to do a little decompilation which may take a few tries to fully get the code, if I recall ILCPP encrypted games takes a while and you might not get functionable code, but it’s step one.   
That just popping in my head, there’s a lot more ways to fix the game without remaking it, mods could be one option too

replies.author: M4ldarc
replies.body: as i have said before, THE FULL GAME CODE is aviable as a mod, the "game" is just the engine running the mod of the real game, but all the code for items, textures, interactions and anything not managed by the engine is aviable in the game files in a folder

replies.author: JJBareaIsLeFather
replies.body: You don't even need the full game code, just the game files to decomp. For something like Stonehearth it's a trivial task. You could have something playable in a couple days, easily.

replies.author: M4ldarc
replies.body: Do i need to do or set up something in specific? I don't belive i can just drop 1gb of files in the bowser gemini chat and have it start working

replies.author: JJBareaIsLeFather
replies.body:
I don't know specifically about Gemni, I use Claude and GPT only. However, it should be basically the same I would imagine. 

Download all the game files and any content you want on Steam/wherever you donwload your games from. 

Make a folder on your drive for the Stonehearth project and copy all the game files from the Stonehearth directory into it. Set the entire folder and all files in it to read only mode. 

Start a project in your AI interface. Give the project access to the project folder you have copied all the Stonehearth files into. 

Have a brief conversation with another AI instance and tell it what you want to do and have it make a plan, work through all the details ahead of time. Tell it you want to make an open source redev path of a new game inspired by Stonehearth and decomp the Stonehearth files to reverse engineer the game. Have that AI generate a roadmap, project overview, and plan out various phases of the project. Make sure you and your planning AI are on the same page before you move forward. 

Then when you get all the details for the project settled and tell it where the project lives on your drive, have that AI produce you the first prompt and feed that prompt and the design documents into your Stonehearth project AI. The project AI will probably ask you to accept it downloading some tools then should begin automatically working. When it finishes, take it's output text, copy it back into the other AI and have the AI evaluate the progress of the project and make the next prompt to feed back in to continue.

comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
Tbh, probs no one quite understands what is going on there, just from this description.

Unless someone owns this game and can check how it is structured, there is no way to know, what is happening and where, how much is hardcoded into engine , how much is delegated to moddable files, what format are they etc.  
Also, it seems it has in-house engine on C++, which is harder to quickly disassemble with AI, compared to Unity or Godot, and it also means, it harder to imagine what exactly is hardcoded and what is not.

If you have game installed, use Claude to go through the game files, to give you overview of formats, ways to work with those files, and then see if there is software or AI plugins to work with those files.   
Maybe you don\`t even need to touch source code, maybe it just jsons, or some lua scripts, then it is easy to use AI on them.  
  
If working on those files is not enough, then you can get CheatEngine to work with game memory first.   
  
After that you can switch to Ghidra + Claude to attempt disassembly (but I am not sure how much AI can carry in custom engines without some user expertise, but you can try, I guess)

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: You can do pretty much whatever you want with software you legally own, as long as you're not distributing it any way, accidentally or intentionally. Want to go put Morrowind in  UE? Go for it. Just don't publish it without contacting Bethesda first. Though there's a slight loophole in that most companies are OK with you doing so as long as your distribution requires the assets of the original game to work (Tale of Two Wastelands did this). So you could make like a UE GFX connector (like they did for Oblivion or for Diablo 2 Remastered) and distribute and be fine since you're not packaging any of the original program in there.
